meta.subtitle: 24x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 (1.5 TB) - Tyrone MDA200A2N-224
meta.platform: Tyrone MDA200A2N-224 / 2x AMD EPYC 9135 (32C/64T, Zen 5 Turin)

executive_summary: 20-minute rapid memory revalidation of 24x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 Registered ECC DIMMs (1.5 TB total) in server 172.16.11.132 (Tyrone MDA200A2N-224, dual AMD EPYC 9135 Zen 5). Core phase: a 5-minute 100% memory burn - stress-ng held 1373 GB (91% of RAM) resident across 64 workers with --vm-method all --verify, completing 1.56 billion verified operations - followed by aggregate, single-thread and NUMA bandwidth benchmarks. Total campaign 13m 48s.

All 24 DIMMs are detected and trained at their full module-rated 5600 MT/s on all 24 channels (1 DPC, 12 channels per socket). Zero ECC errors (CE=0/UE=0 on both UMC controllers), zero machine-check events, zero new BMC SEL entries and zero swap/OOM activity during the burn. Cores sustained full boost throughout the load - peak 4346 MHz against the 4300 MHz rated maximum.

Aggregate stream bandwidth measured 581 GB/s - 31% above the half-populated sibling .217 (443 GB/s, same dual EPYC 9135 platform) - because full 24-of-24 channel population more than offsets the lower 5600 MT/s module clock. Single-thread memcpy 23.8 GB/s; NUMA-remote penalty 1.60x (family norm). The 1.5 TB configuration is revalidated for production memory-bound workloads.

comparison.caption: Same dual EPYC 9135 platform family - this .132 populates all 24 channels with 5600 MT/s modules; sibling .217 runs 12 DIMMs at 6000 MT/s.
comparison.notes: Full channel population wins: despite a 7% lower DIMM clock (5600 vs 6000 MT/s), 24-of-24 channels deliver ~31% more aggregate stream bandwidth than the half-populated sibling (581 vs 443 GB/s). Zen 5 single-thread memcpy is strong on both (23.8 vs 20.8 GB/s) and the 2-socket NUMA-remote penalty is essentially identical (1.60x vs 1.67x) - the Infinity Fabric behaves the same across the family.

sel_status: BMC SEL: 0 new entries during the campaign (279 before and after; last entry 06:21 UTC, pre-test boot).
dmesg_status: 0 machine-check events during the 14-minute window (kernel MCE keyword count unchanged at the single benign boot line). AMD EDAC enumerated 2 memory controllers; CE=0 / UE=0 before and after the burn. Core clocks sampled every 20 s under load: 3974-4346 MHz (rated boost 4300) - no thermal or firmware throttle. Swap untouched; no OOM-killer activity.
findings: All 24 Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 modules are electrically healthy under maximum pressure: the 5-minute 100% burn held 1373 GB (91% of 1511 GB) resident for the entire window while stress-ng's full pattern sweep with --verify completed 1,562,412,338 operations - zero verification failures, zero OOM kills, swap untouched.

ECC and platform logs are spotless: both AMD UMC EDAC controllers read CE=0 / UE=0 before and after; the machine-check count is unchanged; BMC SEL stayed at 279 entries (last entry 06:21 UTC, from the pre-test boot). The box had been freshly rebooted ~24 minutes before the campaign.

BIOS trains every module at the full module rating of 5600 MT/s on all 24 channels (1 DPC). The EPYC 9005 platform itself supports 6000 MT/s at 1 DPC, so the only headroom left is module choice, not training health.

Per-module identity recorded for traceability: all 24 modules are identical Samsung M321R8GA0PB0-CWMCJ, dual-rank, 80-bit total width (64-bit data + 16-bit ECC), Registered (Buffered), serials 80CE04254642E0xxxx (one production lot) - full slot-by-slot map with serial numbers in the Hardware Inventory section.

Bandwidth is the best in the fleet family: 581 GB/s aggregate stream (64 instances, 256 MB DRAM-bound working set), +31% over the half-populated sibling .217 (443 GB/s) despite the slower DIMM clock. DRAM-bound sysbench (1 GiB private blocks per thread) adds 355 GB/s read / 206 GB/s write aggregate; mbw single-thread memcpy is 23.8 GB/s.
NUMA topology is healthy: node0->node0 memcpy 22.5 GiB/s vs node0->node1 14.1 GiB/s - a 1.60x remote penalty, matching the .217 reference (1.67x).

Methodology note: stress-ng's default cache detection on EPYC reads one CCD's 16 MiB L3, which makes the default --stream run cache-resident (it reported an inflated 1.39 TB/s). The corrected run pins --stream-l3-size 256M; sysbench's default shared-buffer write similarly understates (11.8 GB/s) and was rerun with private 1 GiB blocks per thread.
recommendations: Modules cleared for production - no DIMM action required; the 1.5 TB / 24-channel configuration is revalidated for memory-bound workloads (in-memory DBs, virtualization, HPC pre/post-processing).
Optional +7% peak bandwidth: 6000 MT/s-rated modules would let this 1 DPC platform train higher; not required - full population already out-delivers the faster-clocked half-populated sibling.
Install rasdaemon and enable BIOS patrol scrub for continuous per-DIMM error history between validation campaigns.
For future quick campaigns on EPYC, pin stress-ng --stream-l3-size 256M and use sysbench with private 1 GiB blocks - the tool defaults measure cache, not DRAM, on this CPU family.
When the box can be spared, run the full 3-hour qualification tier (as on .41/.217) to add the memtester near-full-residency burn and an extended soak.

reproducibility.bandwidth: stress-ng --stream 64 --stream-l3-size 256M (30 s) -> 581.1 GB/s; sysbench memory 1 GiB blocks/thread, scope=local, 64T: read 355 / write 206 GB/s; mbw -n 3 1024 (1T) -> 23.8 GB/s
reproducibility.numa: numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind={0,1} mbw -n 2 2048 -> 22.5 vs 14.1 GiB/s memcpy = 1.60x remote penalty
reproducibility.edac: AMD EDAC (2 UMC controllers); /sys/devices/system/edac ce_count + ue_count diffed pre/post; dmesg + ipmitool sel info diffed
reproducibility.cpu_freq: /proc/cpuinfo MHz sampled every 20 s during the burn (peak 4345.8 MHz); turbostat post-check (Bzy_MHz 2338, 182 W package, idle recovery)
